title: Ibn Jubayr's Pilgrimage to Mecca and Back
intro: Ibn Jubayr, an Arab geographer, traveller and poet from al-Andalus and secretary to the Almohad governor of Granada, left Granada on 3 February 1183 to make the pilgrimage to Mecca. His chronicle of the journey describes Saladin's domains and, on the way home, Christian Sicily.
ending: He returned by way of Sicily, where a shipwreck at Messina interrupted his voyage, and reached Granada on 25 April 1185. His chronicle became a foundation of the genre called Rihla. His stops also included Medina, Mecca, Damascus, Mosul and Baghdad, which are not drawn here.

stops.text: Ibn Jubayr set out from Granada, where he had been secretary to the Almohad governor, accompanied by a physician from the city. He does not explain his reason for making the pilgrimage.
stops.quote: He left Granada on 3 February 1183 accompanied by a physician from the city.

stops.text: He crossed the Strait of Gibraltar to Ceuta, then under Muslim rule, and boarded a Genoese ship bound for Alexandria.
stops.quote: Ibn Jubayr left Granada and crossed over the Strait of Gibraltar to Ceuta, then under Muslim rule. He boarded a Genoese ship on February 24, 1183 and set sail for Alexandria.

stops.text: The ship passed the Balearic Islands and reached the west coast of Sardinia. Offshore, Ibn Jubayr heard of 80 Muslim men, women and children abducted from North Africa and about to be sold as slaves. A severe storm followed between Sardinia and Sicily.
stops.quote: His sea journey took him past the Balearic Islands and then across to the west coast of Sardinia. Offshore, he heard of the fate of 80 Muslim men, women and children who had been abducted from North Africa and were being sold into slavery.

stops.text: After passing Sicily and Crete, the ship reached the North African coast. At Alexandria customs officials took zakat from the pilgrims, and Ibn Jubayr visited the Lighthouse, then still standing. He stayed eight days.
stops.quote: He arrived in Alexandria on March 26.

stops.text: He reached Cairo three days after leaving Alexandria. He visited the cemetery at al-Qarafah, saw the citadel walls being extended under Saladin, a bridge over the Nile being built, a free hospital, the pyramids and the Sphinx.
stops.quote: He reached Cairo three days later. In the city, he visited the cemetery at al-Qarafah, which contained the graves of many important figures in the history of Islam.

legs.title: Home by way of Acre and Sicily

stops.text: On the return journey Ibn Jubayr passed through the Kingdom of Jerusalem and described Acre. He spent 32 days in the kingdom, thirteen of them anchored in the port of Acre awaiting a favourable wind.
stops.quote: Thirteen of these days were spent anchored in the port of Acre, awaiting a favorable wind.

stops.text: He reached Norman Sicily after a shipwreck in the harbour of Messina, which he survived. He then travelled through the cities of Messina and Palermo.
stops.quote: Il regagne finalement Grenade le 25 avril 1185 après avoir survécu à un naufrage dans le port de Messine.

stops.text: In Sicily, late in his travels, he described Palermo as the metropolis of the island, an ancient city built in the Cordova style of cut stone, where Christian women followed the fashion of Muslim women.

stops.text: Ibn Jubayr reached Granada again on 25 April 1185, after surviving the shipwreck at Messina, and so ended the pilgrimage that had begun two years earlier.
stops.quote: Il regagne finalement Grenade le 25 avril 1185 après avoir survécu à un naufrage dans le port de Messine.

notes: Order is stated for: Granada, Ceuta, Sardinia (west coast), Alexandria, Cairo (EN: 'He reached Cairo three days later'); on the return, Acre then Sicily (FR: 'Lors de son voyage de retour, Ibn Jubair décrit la ville d'Acre ... ainsi que la Sicile normande où il aborda après un naufrage et parcourut les villes de Messine et de Palerme'), Messina (shipwreck in its port) then Palermo, then Granada on 25 April 1185 (FR). Left out: Stromboli (EN has no order relative to Palermo), Sicily and Crete passed at sea (nothing happened there), Medina, Mecca, Damascus, Mosul, Baghdad, Basra, Tibnin (no order, no event). Dates null: Sardinia, Cairo, Acre, Messina. The two sources differ: English says he left in 1183 and the Sicily stay was December 1184 to January 1185; French dates the pilgrimage 1184-1185 and says a month in Jerusalem. The 1183 start is kept; the French dating is not used and is not mentioned in the text. French also says 'Jerusalem' where English says 32 days in the Kingdom of Jerusalem. The Sardinia stop is the sea off its west coast, as the source says.
